benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Rebounded to about $105.88 on 3 Nov (Trading Economics), up roughly 1% on the day, after a US official confirmed to Reuters that US forces struck Iran's Qeshm Island, which officials called a defensive response to Iranian fire on US assets; both benchmarks had fallen more than 7% the prior session as Trump signaled more time for diplomacy (Reuters, via NTD). A senior Iranian official told Reuters the two sides remain far from a deal. Week-ago is this site's 2 Nov reading, 1 day earlier.

note: Brent, WTI and TTF all rebounded modestly on 3 November after a US official confirmed to Reuters that US forces struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, in what officials called a defensive response to Iranian fire on US assets. Both oil benchmarks had fallen more than 7% the prior session after Trump signaled he wants more time for Iran diplomacy before considering further strikes. A senior Iranian official told Reuters the two sides remain far from a deal; the moves came on the day of the 3 November US midterm elections.
